title: Phase 1: Minimal Viable Bridge
description:
The first end-to-end milestone: send a text message in a Telegram forum topic, receive a Claude Code response back in the same topic. This phase produces both running components (proxy + bridge) but with minimal features — text only, no streaming, no media, basic commands.

## Why this is the first milestone
Every subsequent phase adds capabilities (streaming, media, topic lifecycle) on top of this working pipeline. Getting the full roundtrip working first (Telegram → proxy → bridge → Claude CLI → bridge → proxy → Telegram) validates the architecture and data contract before investing in features.

## What this phase intentionally excludes
- No streaming (wait for full response)
- No media processing (text only)
- No topic lifecycle management (no auto-create, no status colors, no pinned metadata)
- No model selection (hardcoded default)
- Single user (admin only)
- No self-updating

## Deliverable
Working text-in, text-out bridge with topic-based conversation isolation. A message in a Telegram forum topic gets a Claude response in the same topic, and conversation context persists across messages via --resume.

title: Implement bridge: session manager (text-only, no streaming)
description:
The session manager that invokes Claude Code CLI for each message.

## Phase 1 scope
- Text-only input (no media)
- No streaming — use --output-format json, wait for full response
- Session creation and resumption via --resume

## Implementation
- On new session: invoke claude -p --output-format json --cwd <dir> with prompt via stdin
  - Parse response JSON: extract session_id, result, is_error, total_cost_usd
  - Store session_id in SQLite
- On existing session: invoke claude -p --output-format json --resume <session_id> --cwd <dir>
- One active subprocess per topic — if a message arrives while Claude is processing, queue it
- Queue implementation: per-topic channel with buffer (capacity 32)
- Queued messages are batched into the next prompt: "Previous messages while processing:\n\n[msg1]\n[msg2]\n\nLatest message:\n[msg3]"
- Timeout: context.WithTimeout (default 300s from group config), kill subprocess on timeout
- On error: send error message to topic, leave session intact for retry
- Model resolution: sessions.model > groups.default_model > "claude-sonnet-4-6"

## CLI invocation pattern
```go
cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "claude", "-p",
    "--output-format", "json",
    "--resume", sessionID, // omit for first invocation
    "--cwd", projectDir,
    "--permission-mode", "plan",
)
cmd.Stdin = strings.NewReader(prompt)
stdout, _ := cmd.Output()
```

## Considerations
- Prompt MUST go via stdin (not as CLI argument) to prevent shell injection from user text
- The first invocation (no --resume) returns a session_id that must be captured and stored
- Claude Code sessions persist on disk in ~/.claude/ — the bridge just needs the session_id to resume
- --permission-mode plan means Claude will propose changes but the CLI will auto-approve in -p mode (non-interactive). Consider whether this is the desired behavior or if we need --permission-mode dontAsk for Phase 1 simplicity.

New sessions: claude -p --output-format json --cwd <dir> via stdin; session_id captured and stored. Existing sessions: --resume <session_id>. Queued messages batched with structured formatting. Timeout from group.timeout_sec. Model resolution chain. Uses --permission-mode bypassPermissions.

title: Implement bridge: sender module
description:
HTTP client that sends responses back through the proxy.

## Implementation
- POST to proxy /send endpoint with the response text, chat_id, thread_id, reply_to_message_id
- Handle message chunking: if response > 4096 chars, split at paragraph boundaries
- First chunk is a reply to the user's message (reply_to_message_id set)
- Subsequent chunks are standalone messages in the same topic (thread_id set, no reply_to)
- Handle proxy errors: retry with backoff on connection failure, respect 429 retry_after
- Store sent message_id in SQLite sent_messages table (for future edit-in-place streaming)
- Send typing indicator (POST /send_chat_action) before dispatching to Claude

## Chunking algorithm (Phase 1, simple)
1. If text ≤ 4096 chars → send as-is
2. Find the last paragraph break (\n\n) before the 4096 limit
3. If no paragraph break, find the last newline (\n)
4. If no newline, split at 4096 (hard cut)
5. Send first chunk, repeat for remaining text

## Considerations
- Phase 1 does not do markdown→HTML conversion (plain text responses)
- The sender should be rate-limit aware: track sends per chat, per group, and global
- The typing indicator auto-expires after 5s — for long Claude responses, the session manager should re-send it every 4s

title: Implement proxy: Telegram long-polling
description:
Core proxy functionality: poll Telegram for updates and normalize them into the data contract envelope format.

## Implementation
- Main loop: call getUpdates with timeout=30, offset=last_update_id+1
- Parse Telegram Update objects into the normalized envelope (internal/contract types)
- Handle all message types: text, photo, voice, audio, video, video_note, document
- Handle callback_query updates
- Handle service messages: forum_topic_created, forum_topic_edited, forum_topic_closed, forum_topic_reopened
- Photo resolution selection: pick the best resolution ≤1280px on long edge
- Store the bot token from env var BOT_TOKEN (injected by OpenBao/k8s secret)

## Key behaviors
- On Telegram API error, log and retry with backoff
- On 409 Conflict (another instance polling), log fatal — only one proxy instance allowed
- Track offset internally — updates are acknowledged when the next getUpdates call includes offset=last+1
- The proxy must NOT interpret message content — it normalizes structure but treats text/media as opaque

## Endpoints implemented in this task
- GET /updates?timeout=30 — returns normalized update envelopes
- GET /health — returns polling status, last_update_id, uptime, contract_version

## Testing
- Unit test: Telegram Update JSON → normalized envelope conversion for each message type
- Integration test: mock Telegram API server, verify polling loop and offset tracking

title: Implement proxy: file download endpoint
description:
Proxy endpoint for the bridge to download files referenced in updates.

## Endpoint
- GET /file/{file_id} — calls Telegram getFile to get file_path, then downloads from https://api.telegram.org/file/bot<token>/<file_path>

## Implementation
- Two-step: getFile returns a file_path, then fetch the actual bytes from the file URL
- Stream the response (don't buffer entire file in memory)
- Set Content-Type from the file's MIME type
- Set Content-Disposition with original filename if available
- Return 404 if file_id is invalid or expired (Telegram file links expire after ~1 hour)
- Return 413 if file exceeds 20MB (Telegram standard bot API limit)

## Considerations
- Not needed for Phase 1 MVP (text-only), but including it here because the endpoint is simple and photo/voice support in Phase 3 depends on it
- Files are NOT cached by the proxy — each request fetches fresh from Telegram
- The bridge should download files promptly after receiving the update since Telegram file URLs expire

- Icon color presets: 0x6FB9F0 (blue), 0xFFD67E (yellow), 0xCB86DB (purple), 0x8EEE98 (green), 0xFF93B2 (pink), 0xFB6F5F (red)

- These endpoints are needed for Phase 4 (topic lifecycle) but the /answer_callback is needed for Phase 2 (permission handling via inline keyboards)
- Bot must have can_manage_topics permission in the group
- /pin_message should support disable_notification=true to avoid spamming the group

- service.yaml — ClusterIP service exposing port 8080 (or use Tailscale directly)

The proxy pod needs to be reachable from EX44 over Tailscale. Options:
1. Tailscale sidecar container in the pod — pod gets its own Tailscale IP
2. Tailscale ingress via existing cluster Tailscale setup — route through Traefik or similar
3. HostNetwork + node's Tailscale — simplest but less isolated

- curl http://telegram-proxy:8080/updates?timeout=5 from EX44 returns an empty updates array (or real updates if messages have been sent)
- Send a message in the Telegram group, curl /updates shows it

## Considerations
- The ArgoCD Application should be in the ardenone-cluster's app-of-apps or standalone
- Resource limits are generous for this workload — the proxy is ~10MB binary doing HTTP I/O
- Liveness probe: GET /health every 30s
- No PVC needed — the proxy is stateless (offset tracked in memory, lost on restart is OK since Telegram retains unacked updates for 24h)

title: Implement bridge: poller module
description:
The poller goroutine that fetches updates from the proxy.

## Implementation
- Goroutine running pollLoop(): call GET /updates?timeout=30 in a loop
- Deserialize response into []contract.Update
- Dispatch each update to the router via a channel or direct call
- On connection error: exponential backoff (1s, 2s, 4s, 8s... max 30s), reset on success
- On HTTP timeout (expected after 30s with no updates): just retry immediately
- Configurable proxy URL from config

## Considerations
- The poller should use a context.Context for clean shutdown
- The HTTP client timeout should be longer than the poll timeout (e.g., 35s) to avoid client-side timeouts before the proxy responds
- If the proxy returns an error response (502, 503), treat it like a connection error (backoff)
- Log connection state transitions (connected, disconnected, reconnected) at INFO level

title: Implement bridge: router module
description:
The router that dispatches updates to the appropriate handler based on (chat_id, thread_id).

## Implementation
- Receive updates from the poller
- Check from_user.id against allowed_users table — silently drop unauthorized messages
- Classify the update:
  - type == "callback_query" → dispatch to session that owns the callback
  - type == "service" → dispatch to topic lifecycle handler
  - thread_id is nil or 1 (General topic) AND content is a command → dispatch to command handler
  - thread_id is non-nil, non-1 → look up (chat_id, thread_id) in sessions table
    - Found → dispatch to session manager with existing session info
    - Not found → check groups table for chat_id, if registered create new session, else ignore

## Considerations
- The General topic detection: thread_id can be nil (message sent without thread context) or 1 (explicit General topic). Both should route to the command handler if the message starts with /
- Command detection: check if the first entity in content.entities is type "bot_command" at offset 0, or simpler: check if text starts with /
- The router is the security boundary — unauthorized messages must be dropped here before reaching any handler
- For unknown groups (chat_id not in groups table): silently ignore. Groups must be registered first via /cwd in General topic.

title: Implement bridge: SQLite state module
description:
SQLite database for routing state, session tracking, and user authorization.

## Schema (from plan)
```sql
CREATE TABLE groups (
    chat_id       INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    name          TEXT,
    cwd           TEXT NOT NULL,
    default_model TEXT DEFAULT 'claude-sonnet-4-6',
    max_budget    REAL DEFAULT 5.0,
    timeout_sec   INTEGER DEFAULT 300,
    created_at    TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now'))
);

CREATE TABLE sessions (
    chat_id       INTEGER NOT NULL,
    thread_id     INTEGER NOT NULL,
    session_id    TEXT NOT NULL,
    cwd           TEXT NOT NULL,
    model         TEXT,
    status        TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active',
    created_at    TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now')),
    last_active   TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now')),
    message_count INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    PRIMARY KEY (chat_id, thread_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (chat_id) REFERENCES groups(chat_id)

CREATE TABLE allowed_users (
    user_id       INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    role          TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'user',
    added_at      TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now'))
);

CREATE TABLE sent_messages (
    chat_id       INTEGER NOT NULL,
    thread_id     INTEGER NOT NULL,
    message_id    INTEGER NOT NULL,
    purpose       TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_at    TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now')),
    PRIMARY KEY (chat_id, thread_id, message_id)
);
```

## Implementation
- Use modernc.org/sqlite (pure Go, no CGo)
- Enable WAL mode for concurrent read/write
- Schema versioning: a schema_version table tracking applied migrations
- Migrations run on startup, idempotent and forward-only
- CRUD methods for each table: GetGroup, UpsertGroup, GetSession, CreateSession, UpdateSession, etc.
- Transaction support for operations that touch multiple tables

## Considerations
- Database file location: configurable, default to ./data/bridge.db
- WAL mode prevents "database is locked" errors from concurrent goroutines
- The initial admin user should be configurable (env var or config file) so the first /cwd command works
- All timestamps stored as ISO 8601 strings (SQLite doesn't have a native datetime type)

title: Phase 4: Topic Lifecycle and Operations
description:
Automate topic management and add operational visibility. Topics become self-describing (pinned metadata), self-organizing (status colors), and self-cleaning (TTL). The bridge becomes observable via monitoring and health checks.

## Why this phase matters
Without lifecycle management, topics accumulate without context — you can't tell which are active, what model they're using, or what project they belong to without opening each one. Status colors and pinned metadata give at-a-glance visibility. Session cleanup prevents stale sessions from consuming resources.

## Deliverable
Self-managing topic lifecycle with status colors, pinned metadata, auto-creation, session cleanup, and operational monitoring.

title: Implement topic auto-creation via /new command
description:
The /new command creates a Telegram topic and registers a Claude session in one step.

## Implementation
- /new [name] in General topic:
  1. Call POST /create_topic on the proxy with the name and default icon color (blue = active)
  2. Receive thread_id from the response
  3. Create a new entry in the sessions table
  4. Invoke claude -p to create the session and capture session_id
  5. Pin the metadata message (session_id, cwd, model, start time)
  6. Reply in General topic: "Created topic: {name} (thread_id: {id})"

## Considerations
- The topic name should be the task description (e.g., "fix auth middleware")
- If no name is provided, prompt the user to provide one
- The initial Claude prompt should include the topic name as context: "New task: {name}. How can I help?"
- Icon color defaults to light blue (0x6FB9F0 = active)

title: Implement topic status colors
description:
Update topic icon colors based on session state.

## Color mapping
| Status | Color | Hex | When |
|--------|-------|-----|------|
| Active | Light blue | 0x6FB9F0 | Session is processing or idle and active |
| Complete | Green | 0x8EEE98 | Topic closed via /close or Telegram UI |
| Blocked | Yellow | 0xFFD67E | Claude hit a permission prompt or error that needs user input |
| Error | Red/orange | 0xFB6F5F | Claude subprocess failed or timed out |
| Review | Pink | 0xFF93B2 | Claude proposed changes awaiting review |
| Research | Purple | 0xCB86DB | Could be set manually for research-type tasks |

## Implementation
- After each Claude invocation: if error → red, if success → blue
- On topic close: green
- On timeout: red
- Color changes via POST /edit_topic to the proxy
- Store current color in sessions table (new column: icon_color)

## Considerations
- Don't change color on every message — only on state transitions
- The user should be able to manually set colors too (topic-level command /color [name])
- Telegram only supports 6 preset colors — we can't use custom colors

title: Implement pinned metadata messages
description:
Pin a metadata message in each topic showing session info.

## Content
```
Session: abc123
Project: ~/telegram-claude-bridge
Model: claude-sonnet-4-6 (group default)
Started: 2026-04-04 10:30 UTC
Messages: 12
Cost: $0.34
```

## Implementation
- On session creation: send a message to the topic with metadata, then POST /pin_message with disable_notification=true
- Store the pinned message_id in sessions table (new column: pinned_message_id)
- On model change (/model, /haiku, /sonnet, /opus, or natural language): POST /edit to update the pinned message
- On each Claude response: update message_count and cost in the pinned message (debounce: at most once per minute)

## Considerations
- The pinned message provides at-a-glance context when you open a topic
- Cost is parsed from the stream-json result event's total_cost_usd field
- Updating too frequently wastes API calls — debounce to once per minute or on significant changes
- The pin notification is disabled to avoid spamming the group

title: Implement session cleanup and TTL
description:
Clean up stale sessions to prevent unbounded growth.

## Implementation
- Background goroutine runs every hour
- Query sessions where last_active < now - TTL (configurable, default 7 days)
- For stale sessions:
  1. Update status to "inactive" in SQLite
  2. Optionally close the Telegram topic (POST /close_topic) — configurable
  3. Update topic color to green (complete)
  4. Log the cleanup

## Considerations
- TTL should be configurable per group (some projects have long-running tasks)
- Closing topics is optional — some users may want to keep them open for reference
- The cleanup should NOT delete session data — just mark as inactive and optionally close the topic
- Claude Code sessions persist on disk independently — they can always be resumed even after cleanup
- /sessions command should show inactive sessions with an "inactive" label

title: Implement bridge health monitoring
description:
Health checks and operational monitoring for the bridge.

## Implementation
1. Bridge exposes a local HTTP health endpoint (localhost:9091/health) for systemd watchdog or external monitoring
2. Health check verifies:
   - Proxy reachable (GET /health returns ok)
   - SQLite writable (insert and delete a test row)

```

title: Implement topic-level model selection commands
description:
Model selection within individual topics, including natural language switching.

## Topic commands
- /model [name] — view or set model for this topic (overrides group default)
- /haiku — shortcut for claude-haiku-4-5
- /sonnet — shortcut for claude-sonnet-4-6
- /opus — shortcut for claude-opus-4-6
- /info — show session info (model, cwd, session_id, cost, messages)

## Natural language detection
Before dispatching a message to Claude, check for model-change phrases:
- strings.ToLower() the message text
- strings.Contains() against a table of known phrases:
  - "use opus", "switch to opus" → claude-opus-4-6
  - "use sonnet", "switch to sonnet" → claude-sonnet-4-6
  - "use haiku", "switch to haiku" → claude-haiku-4-5
  - "think harder", "this needs more power" → escalate one tier
  - "quick answer", "keep it simple" → de-escalate one tier

## Model resolution order
1. sessions.model (topic-level override)
2. groups.default_model (group-level default)
3. "claude-sonnet-4-6" (hardcoded fallback)

## Implementation
- On model change: update sessions.model in SQLite, update pinned metadata, reply with confirmation
- If message has text beyond the model-change phrase, strip the phrase and forward remainder to Claude
- If message is ONLY a model change request, no Claude invocation

## Considerations
- The phrase table must be specific enough to avoid false positives. "opus" alone shouldn't trigger — need "use opus" or "switch to opus"
- De-escalation: haiku can't go lower, opus can't go higher. Inform the user if already at the limit.

title: Phase 3: Media Processing
description:
Handle non-text inputs from Telegram: images, voice messages, audio files, documents, and optionally video. This phase transforms the bridge from text-only to multi-modal, letting users send screenshots for Claude to analyze, voice messages that get transcribed, and documents for Claude to read.

## Why multi-modal matters
The most common use case beyond text is sending a screenshot of an error or a code snippet and asking "what's wrong here?" Voice messages are natural on mobile. Document support lets users upload specs, configs, or code files.

## Media pipeline
All media flows through the same pipeline:
1. Bridge receives update with media content (file_id in the envelope)
2. Bridge downloads the file from proxy via GET /file/{file_id}
3. Bridge preprocesses if needed (resize images, transcribe audio, extract video frames)
4. Bridge includes the file path or transcription in the prompt to Claude
5. Claude uses its Read tool to process the file

## Deliverable
Full multi-modal input: images analyzed by Claude, voice transcribed to text, documents passed through, video keyframes + transcription.

title: Implement proxy: media send endpoints
description:
Add media send endpoints to the proxy for the bridge to send files back to Telegram.

## Endpoints
- POST /send_photo — sendPhoto (multipart: chat_id, thread_id, photo file, caption, parse_mode)
- POST /send_document — sendDocument (multipart: chat_id, thread_id, document file, caption, file_name)
- POST /send_audio — sendAudio (multipart: chat_id, thread_id, audio file, caption, duration, title)
- POST /send_video — sendVideo (multipart: chat_id, thread_id, video file, caption, duration, width, height)

## Implementation
- Accept multipart/form-data requests
- Forward to Telegram API with bot token injected
- Return {ok: true, message_id: ...}
- File size limits: 10MB for photos, 50MB for documents/audio/video

## Considerations

- The proxy should validate file sizes before forwarding to Telegram to give clear error messages

title: Implement bridge: image processing pipeline
description:
Handle photo messages from Telegram.

## Pipeline
1. Update arrives with content.type == "photo"
2. Download file from proxy: GET /file/{content.file_id}
3. Save to /tmp/telegram-bridge/{chat_id}/{message_id}.jpg
4. Resize to ~800px on the long edge (if larger) using Go's image package or imagemagick CLI
5. Build prompt: "[User sent an image: /tmp/telegram-bridge/12345/photo.jpg]\n{caption if present}\nPlease analyze this image."
6. Dispatch to session manager as normal
7. Cleanup: delete temp file after Claude finishes processing

## Image resizing
Option A: Use Go's image/jpeg and golang.org/x/image/draw packages (no external dependency)
Option B: Shell out to imagemagick (convert input.jpg -resize 800x800> output.jpg)

Prefer Option A for fewer dependencies. The resize is simple: if max(width, height) > 800, scale proportionally.

## Considerations
- Claude Code's Read tool can process JPEG and PNG images natively
- Token cost: ~1334 tokens per 1000x1000 image. Resizing to 800px saves tokens.
- Captions from photos should be included in the prompt text
- If the photo has a caption, combine: "[Image: path]\nCaption: {caption}\n"
- Multiple photos in one message: Telegram sends each as a separate update. Process sequentially.

title: Implement bridge: voice/audio transcription pipeline
description:
Handle voice messages and audio files from Telegram.

## Pipeline
1. Update arrives with content.type == "voice" or "audio"
2. Download file from proxy: GET /file/{content.file_id}
3. Save to /tmp/telegram-bridge/{chat_id}/{message_id}.ogg (voice) or .mp3/.m4a (audio)
4. Transcribe via Whisper CLI: whisper /tmp/file.ogg --model turbo --output_format txt --output_dir /tmp/telegram-bridge/{chat_id}/
5. Read transcription from output file
6. Build prompt: "[Voice message transcription]: {transcription text}\n\nPlease respond to the above."
7. Dispatch to session manager
8. Cleanup temp files

## Whisper invocation
```go
cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "whisper",
    filepath.Join(tmpDir, filename),
    "--model", "turbo",
    "--output_format", "txt",
    "--output_dir", tmpDir,
)
```

## Considerations
- Whisper handles OGG/Opus (Telegram voice format) natively via ffmpeg
- whisper CLI must be installed on EX44: pip install openai-whisper (this is the one Python dependency)
- Alternatively: use faster-whisper or whisper.cpp for lower latency and no Python dependency
- Whisper turbo model is ~6GB download on first run — ensure disk space
- For audio files with a title (e.g., meeting-notes.mp3), include the title in the prompt
- Transcription can be slow (10-30s for long messages). Send a typing indicator while processing.
- Consider sending the transcription back to the user for verification: "Transcription: {text}\nSending to Claude..." — opt-in via config

title: Implement bridge: document handling pipeline
description:
Handle document uploads from Telegram.

## Pipeline
1. Update arrives with content.type == "document"
2. Download from proxy: GET /file/{content.file_id}
3. Save to /tmp/telegram-bridge/{chat_id}/{message_id}_{file_name}
4. Classify by MIME type:
   - Text/code (text/*, application/json, application/yaml, etc.): pass directly to Claude via file path
   - PDF (application/pdf): pass directly — Claude's Read tool handles PDFs
   - Image (image/*): pass directly — Claude's Read tool handles images
   - Jupyter notebook (.ipynb): pass directly
   - Unsupported (Office docs, archives, binaries): notify user "This file type is not directly supported. Claude can process text, code, PDF, and image files."
5. Build prompt: "[User uploaded: {file_name}]\nFile saved to: {path}\n{caption if present}"
6. Dispatch to session manager

## Considerations
- Telegram 20MB download limit via standard Bot API
- Claude's Read tool can handle most text-based files and images natively
- For large PDFs (>10 pages), Claude's Read tool requires page ranges — the prompt should hint at this
- file_name from Telegram should NOT be used as the filesystem path (security) — use generated names with the original extension
- Archive files (.zip, .tar.gz): could extract and pass individual files, but this adds complexity. Defer to Phase 5.

title: Implement bridge: video processing pipeline (stretch)

2. Extract keyframes: ffmpeg -i video.mp4 -vf "fps=0.5,scale=800:-1" frame_%04d.jpg
3. Extract audio track: ffmpeg -i video.mp4 -vn -acodec pcm_s16le audio.wav
4. Transcribe audio via Whisper

- fps=0.5 means one frame every 2 seconds — a 30-second video produces 15 frames
- Each frame costs ~1334 tokens — 15 frames = ~20K tokens. Consider limiting to 5-10 keyframes.
- Video notes (round videos) are short (max 1 min) and lower resolution — simpler case
- This is a stretch goal because video input to Claude is less common than screenshots or voice

title: Implement stream-json NDJSON parser
description:
Parse Claude Code CLI --output-format stream-json output for progressive streaming.

## Implementation
- Switch session manager from --output-format json to --output-format stream-json --include-partial-messages
- Read stdout line-by-line via bufio.Scanner
- Parse each line as JSON, discriminate by "type" field:
  - "system" — init event, contains session info. Extract session_id.
  - "assistant" — complete assistant message blocks (TextBlock, ToolUseBlock)
  - "stream_event" — partial content deltas. Extract text_delta from content_block_delta events.
  - "result" — final metadata: session_id, result, is_error, total_cost_usd, usage

## Go types
```go
type StreamEvent struct {
    Type  string          json:"type"
    Event json.RawMessage json:"event,omitempty"
    // ... other fields per type
}

type ContentBlockDelta struct {
    Type  string json:"type"  // "content_block_delta"
    Index int    json:"index"
    Delta struct {
        Type string json:"type" // "text_delta"
        Text string json:"text"
    } json:"delta"
}
```

## Considerations
- bufio.Scanner has a default max line size of 64KB. Claude responses can exceed this. Set scanner.Buffer() to 1MB.
- stream_event with text_delta gives character-level streaming. Accumulate into a buffer for debounced Telegram edits.
- The result event at the end contains the canonical session_id — use this to update SQLite if it differs from the system event.

title: Implement progressive message editing
description:
Stream Claude's response to Telegram by editing a message in-place.

## Implementation
1. When session starts processing, send a placeholder message ("Thinking...") via POST /send
2. Store the message_id of the placeholder
3. As text_delta events arrive, accumulate into a buffer
4. On a debounce timer (1 edit/second max), POST /edit with the accumulated text so far
5. On completion, send final formatted message (Phase 2.3 markdown→HTML)
6. If accumulated text exceeds 4096 chars during streaming:
   a. Stop editing the current message
   b. Send a new message for overflow content
   c. Continue streaming into the new message

## Debounce implementation
```go
ticker := time.NewTicker(time.Second)
defer ticker.Stop()
for {
    select {
    case delta := <-textDeltas:
        buffer.WriteString(delta)
        dirty = true
    case <-ticker.C:
        if dirty {
            sender.Edit(chatID, msgID, buffer.String())
            dirty = false
        }
    case <-done:
        // final edit with formatted text
        return
    }
}
```

## Considerations
- Telegram silently ignores edits where text hasn't changed (returns 400 "message is not modified"). Treat as no-op.
- The typing indicator (sendChatAction) auto-expires after 5s. During streaming, the edit-in-place IS the visual feedback, so we don't need to re-send typing indicators.
- If the user sends a new message while Claude is still streaming, queue it (existing behavior from Phase 1).

2. Text delta events accumulated in buffer
3. Debounced edits (max 1/second) via streamDebounce constant
4. Overflow handling: when text exceeds 4096 chars, current message is finalized with truncated content and overflow sent as new message
5. Streaming continues into new overflow message
6. Telegram 400 "message is not modified" treated as no-op

title: Implement markdown to HTML converter
description:
Convert Claude's markdown output to Telegram-compatible HTML. ## Supported conversions - **bold** → bold - *italic* → italic - \`code\` → code - \`\`\`language\ncode\n\`\`\` → 
code
- [text](url) → text - ~~strikethrough~~ → strikethrough - > blockquote →
text
- Plain text: escape <, >, & → < > & ## Why HTML over MarkdownV2 MarkdownV2 in Telegram requires escaping 20+ special characters and is notoriously buggy with nested formatting. Every surveyed implementation that tried MarkdownV2 documented it as a pain point. HTML only needs 3 characters escaped (<, >, &) and is far more predictable. ## Implementation - Write a simple state-machine parser (not a full markdown parser) - Process the text in a single pass, maintaining state for: - Inside/outside code block (``` toggles) - Inside/outside inline code (` toggles) - Bold/italic state - Text inside code blocks: only escape HTML entities, don't process markdown - Text outside code blocks: convert markdown formatting to HTML tags ## Considerations - Claude's output can have nested formatting (bold inside italic). Telegram HTML supports this. - Claude sometimes outputs markdown that doesn't perfectly parse (e.g., unmatched asterisks). The converter should be fault-tolerant — unmatched markers are left as literal text. - Code blocks with language tags should set class="language-X" for Telegram's syntax highlighting. - The converter MUST be tested against real Claude output samples — collect test cases from actual Claude responses.

title: Implement permission handling via inline keyboards
description:
Interactive tool approval when Claude runs in --permission-mode plan.

## How it works
When Claude proposes a tool use (file edit, command execution), the stream-json output includes tool_use blocks before the result. In -p mode, Claude auto-proceeds. But we want user approval.

## Implementation options
Option A (recommended for Phase 2): Use --permission-mode acceptEdits or dontAsk, skip interactive approval. This is simpler and matches the solo-operator use case.

Option B (Phase 5): For multi-user, add interactive approval:
1. Detect tool_use blocks in the stream
2. Pause the stream (hold the subprocess)
3. Send an inline keyboard to Telegram: [Approve] [Deny] [Show Details]
4. Wait for callback_query from the user
5. Write y/n to the subprocess stdin
6. Resume streaming

## Phase 2 decision
Go with Option A for now. Set --permission-mode to the group's configured mode. Default to acceptEdits for trusted groups. This avoids the complexity of bidirectional subprocess I/O while still being useful.

## Considerations
- The -p flag in Claude Code runs non-interactively — it doesn't pause for permission prompts the way interactive mode does
- Interactive approval would require NOT using -p and instead managing the full interactive session, which is significantly more complex
- Alternatively, could use --permission-mode plan which shows the plan but auto-approves in -p mode, giving visibility without blocking

title: Phase 9: Dispatcher Architecture
description:
Primary architectural target. The bridge is a dispatcher, not a pipe. Each Telegram topic session is an orchestrator Claude instance that understands user intent, delegates sub-tasks to worker Claude instances via the spawn_worker synthetic tool, and synthesises results. The bridge manages worker lifecycles, routes results back to the thread and orchestrator context, and posts periodic progress updates.

## Orchestrator vs Worker
- Orchestrator: resumed session (--resume session_id), persistent per topic, calls spawn_worker + update_progress tools
- Worker: fresh session (no --resume), short-lived, executes one sub-task, result posted to thread + injected to orchestrator

## Synthetic tools (bridge-intercepted, not real Anthropic tools)
- spawn_worker(prompt, model?) → dispatches goroutine, returns immediately
- update_progress(message) → posts to thread, returns immediately

## Sub-beads
- [x] 9.1: Orchestrator system prompt injection
- [x] 9.2: spawn_worker synthetic tool + WorkerPool
- [x] 9.3: update_progress synthetic tool
- [x] 9.4: Bridge-side progress ticker
- [x] 9.5: Worker result injection on next prompt
- [x] 9.6: Continuous typing indicator

See plan: docs/plan/plan.md (Phase 9 + Session Manager)

title: 9.2: spawn_worker synthetic tool
description:
Bridge intercepts tool_use blocks named 'spawn_worker' from the orchestrator stream, launches a fresh claude -p subprocess, and returns tool_result immediately without blocking the orchestrator.

## Flow
1. Scanner loop in invokeClaudeAPI sees content_block_start with type=tool_use, name=spawn_worker
2. Bridge parses input: {prompt, model?}
3. Inserts workers row (status=running)
4. Returns tool_result to orchestrator stdin immediately: {worker_id, status: dispatched}
5. Spawns goroutine: fresh claude -p (no --resume), inherited CWD, specified model
6. On worker completion:
   - Update workers row to status=done/failed
   - Post to Telegram thread: ⚙️ Worker [N] complete: <truncated result>
   - Add result to pendingWorkerResults[(chatID,threadID)]

## Worker depth limit
Workers cannot call spawn_worker themselves (depth=1 max). Enforce via --disallowed-tools spawn_worker on worker invocations.

2. Parse input: {message}
3. Send message to Telegram thread (new message, not edit of placeholder)
4. Return tool_result to orchestrator stdin: {ok: true}
5. Reset bridge-side progress ticker timer (see 9.4)

Near-zero latency — just an HTTP call to the proxy. Orchestrator is not blocked.

title: 9.5: Worker result injection on next prompt
description:
Completed worker results are prepended to the next prompt sent to the orchestrator, closing the loop so the orchestrator always has access to worker outputs.

## Data flow
- pendingWorkerResults map[(chatID,threadID)] []WorkerResult in SessionManager
- Worker goroutine on completion: append to pendingWorkerResults[(chatID,threadID)]

  Worker 2 (model: sonnet): <result>

  <user message text>

- Drained atomically under SessionManager.mu to avoid race with worker goroutines

## Edge cases
- Worker completes while orchestrator is still running: results queued, injected on next processBatch
- Multiple workers complete before next message: all results prepended together
- Worker fails: include error summary in injection (Worker 1 FAILED: <error>)

title: Phase 6: Self-Updating and Versioning
description:
Self-updating bridge binary, semver versioning, and auto-summary on session close. This phase makes the system self-maintaining and self-documenting.

## Why self-updating matters
The bridge runs on EX44 as a systemd unit. Without self-update, every code change requires SSH → git pull → go build → systemctl restart. With self-update, push to main → bridge detects the change → builds → restarts automatically. This is especially important because Claude Code sessions might be making changes to this very repo.

## Deliverable
Bridge that auto-updates from git, semver in /version command, auto-summary on topic close.

title: Implement bridge self-update mechanism
description:
The bridge periodically checks for new commits and rebuilds itself.

## Update cycle
1. Every 5 minutes (configurable): git -C <repo-path> fetch origin main
2. Compare local HEAD with origin/main — if same, no update needed
3. git -C <repo-path> pull origin main
4. go build -ldflags "..." -o <tmp-binary> ./cmd/bridge/
5. If build succeeds: replace current binary, signal systemd to restart
6. If build fails: log error, notify via Telegram, continue running current binary

## Binary replacement
- Build to a temp file first (e.g., bin/bridge.new)
- os.Rename(bin/bridge.new, bin/bridge) — atomic on same filesystem
- Restart: exec syscall to replace the running process, or systemctl restart telegram-bridge

## Graceful shutdown
- On restart signal: stop accepting new messages from poller
- Wait for active Claude subprocesses to finish (with timeout, e.g., 60s)
- Send "Bridge restarting for update..." to each group's General topic
- Exit with code 0 — systemd restarts with the new binary

## /update command (admin)
- Triggers the update check immediately instead of waiting for the next cycle
- Reports: "Checking for updates..." → "No updates available" or "Updating to {commit}..."

## Considerations
- The Go toolchain must be installed on EX44 for go build to work
- The build uses the same ldflags as CI: version from git describe, commit SHA, build date

title: Implement auto-summary on session close
description:
When a topic is closed, generate a summary and pin it.

## Implementation
1. On topic close (via Telegram UI or /close command):
2. Send a final prompt to the session: "Summarize what was accomplished in this session in 2-3 bullet points. Note any unfinished work or open questions."
3. Wait for response (use --output-format json, not streaming — this is a quick summary)
4. Pin the summary as a new message in the topic
5. Store the summary text in a new column: sessions.summary
6. Mark session as closed in SQLite

## Considerations
- This costs one additional Claude prompt per session close — cheap (Haiku would be ideal for summaries)
- Use the cheapest model available for summary generation regardless of the session's model setting
- The summary should be searchable — store in SQLite and index for /search (future feature)
- If the session has errors or the Claude CLI fails for the summary, skip gracefully and just close without a summary
- The summary is pinned AFTER the topic is closed — Telegram allows pinning in closed topics

title: Implement cost tracking and /cost command
description:
Track Claude API costs per topic and group.

## Data source
Every --output-format json and stream-json result event includes:
- total_cost_usd: float
- usage: {input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read_tokens, cache_creation_tokens}

## Implementation
- New table:
```sql
CREATE TABLE cost_events (
    id          INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    chat_id     INTEGER NOT NULL,
    thread_id   INTEGER NOT NULL,
    cost_usd    REAL NOT NULL,
    input_tokens  INTEGER,
    output_tokens INTEGER,
    model       TEXT,
    created_at  TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now'))
);
```
- After each Claude invocation, insert a cost_event row
- /cost command (General topic): show group total, per-topic breakdown, daily trend
- /cost command (in topic): show this topic's total cost
- Budget enforcement: if cumulative cost > groups.max_budget, warn at 80% and hard-stop at 100%
- On hard-stop: send message "Budget exceeded for this group. Admin can increase via /budget." and reject further messages

## Considerations
- total_cost_usd may be 0 for cached responses — still record the event for usage tracking
- The cost_events table can grow large — consider retention policy (keep 90 days, aggregate older data)
- Cost data in the pinned metadata message updates on each invocation (debounced)

title: 8.1: Cancel intent detection

- If nothing is running: reply "Nothing is currently running"
- If phrase + remaining text: cancel current, then start new invocation with remainder

title: 8.3: Cost and status intent detection

title: 8.4: Session close intent detection
description:
Detect session-end phrases and close the current topic/session.

## Phrases
"close this session" / "close session" / "end session" / "we are done" /
"were done" / "all done" / "finished" / "done here" / "close this topic" /
"shut this down" / "wrap up"

- Update topic color to green (ColorComplete)
- Reply: "Session closed."
- Optionally close the Telegram topic (same as /close)
- Pure intent — do not forward to Claude

## Disambiguation
"finished" is ambiguous — only treat as close intent if it appears alone or at start of message with no other substantial content (len(remainder) < 20 chars after stripping).

title: 8.5: Timeout adjustment intent detection
description:
Detect timeout preference phrases and update session timeout without /timeout command.

## Patterns (require duration extraction)
"set timeout to N minutes" / "timeout N minutes" / "give it N minutes" /
"let it run for N minutes" / "wait up to N hours" / "N minute timeout"

## No-timeout patterns
"no timeout" / "let it run" / "run as long as needed" / "no time limit" /
"run indefinitely" / "dont time out" / "take as long as you need"

## Duration extraction
Parse integer + unit from the phrase:
  "30 minutes" → 1800s
  "1 hour" → 3600s
  "2 hours" → 7200s
  "90 seconds" → 90s
Use a small regex or manual tokenizer — no external dependency.

## Behavior
- Update sessions.timeout_sec (from schema migration in 7.2)
- Reply: "Timeout set to 30 minutes" or "Timeout disabled — session will run indefinitely"
- Update pinned metadata message with new timeout
- If remainder after phrase: forward to Claude with new timeout already applied

title: 8.6: New session/topic intent detection

"start a new conversation" / "new conversation"

Optionally with a name:
"start a new session called X" / "new topic for X" / "new session: X"

## Behavior

- Call the same logic as /new [name] command

Simple: take text after "called", "for", "named", or ":" up to end of message or 50 chars.
